sentences: 1560 Delmar Drive Folcroft, PA 19032 Defendant.

CIVIL ACTION Plaintiff, George Smith, by and through his undersigned attorneys, brings this civil matter against Defendant Southeast Delco School District alleging that he was subjected to unlawful violations of his constitutional rights, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (“Title VII"), the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act (“PHRA”) and 42 U.S.C. $1981, and avers and alleges as follows:.

sections.name: THE PARTIES
sentences: The allegations contained in the foregoing paragraphs of this Complaint are incorporated by reference herein as if the same were set forth at length. i. Case 2:19-cv-03150-CSMW Document1 Filed 07/19/19 Page 5 of 12 Plaintiff George Smith (hereinafter “Plaintiff’) is an African-American man and a practicing Christian. . Plaintiff resides at the above-captioned address.
Defendant Southeast Delco School District (hereinafter “Defendant”) is a school district with a location at the above-captioned address.
Plaintiff was employed by Defendant and worked at or near the above-listed Folcroft, Pennsylvania address from January 2012 until his constructive termination in September of 2018.
At all times relevant hereto, Defendant acted by and through its agents, servants, and employees, each of whom acted within the scope of his or her jobs responsibilities.

sections.name: JURSIDICTION AND VENUE
sentences: The foregoing paragraphs are incorporated by reference herein as ifthe same were set forth at length.

The Court may properly maintain persona! jurisdiction over Defendant because the Defendant’s contacts with this state and this judicial district are sufficient for the exercise of jurisdiction and comply with traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice, thus satisfying the standard set forth by the United States Supreme Court in Jaternational Shoe Co. v. Washington, 326 U.S. 310 (1945) and its progeny.

The Court may exercise original subject-matter jurisdiction over the instant action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331 and 1343(a)(4) because it arises under the laws of the United States and seeks redress for violations of federal law. The Court may also maintain supplemental jurisdiction over state law claims set forth herein pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1367(a) and Rule 18(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure because they are sufficiently related to one or more claims within the Court’s original! jurisdiction that they form part of the same case or controversy.

Venue is properly laid in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1391(b)(1) and 1391(b)(2) because the Defendant is located in this judicial district and because all of the acts and/or omissions giving rise to the claims set forth herein occurred in this judicial district.

sections.name: EXHAUSTION OF ADMINISTRATIVE REMEDIES
sentences: . The foregoing paragraphs are incorporated by reference herein as if the same were set forth at length.
Plaintiff exhausted his administrative remedies under Title VII. Butterbaugh v. Chertoff, 479 F, Supp.

On or around July 13, 2018, Plaintiff filed a timely written Charge of Discrimination (the “Charge”) against Defendant with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”) alleging retaliation and religious discrimination, The charge was duly filed with the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (“PHRC”).

Plaintiff received a Notice of Right to Sue relative to the Charge, by mail, on April 29, Plaintiff files the instant Complaint within ninety (90) days of his receipt of the Notice of Right to Sue letter relative the Charge.

sections.name: FACTUAL SUMMARY
sentences: The allegations contained in the foregoing paragraphs of this Complaint are incorporated by reference herein as if the same were set forth at length.
Plaintiff began working for Defendant in or around January of 2012.
Throughout the majority of his employment with Defendant, Plaintiff served as a Public Safety Officer.
Plaintiff was qualified for his position and performed well.

Throughout the entirety of his employment with Defendant, Plaintiff maintained a second job. Defendant knew about and approved of this job. On or around May 17, 2018, Plaintiff was praying as required by his religion.
Plaintiff's prayers did not interfere with his work.
Employees of other religions were allowed to pray while at work.
Further, employees who were not African-American were allowed to pray while at work.
Case 2:19-cv-03150-CSMW Document1 Filed 07/19/19 Page 7 of 12 Despite this, Plaintiff was confronted by a supervisor, who ordered Plaintiff to refrain from praying at work.
On or around May 18, 2018, Plaintiff submitted a written complaint of race and religious discrimination to Defendant.
Shortly thereafter, on or around June 4, 2018, Plaintiff formally requested that Defendant provide him with a religious accommodation so that Plaintiff could pray at work.
30, Several weeks later, on or around June 22, 2018, without just cause, Defendant demoted Plaintiff to the position of hall monitor.
On or around June 26, 2018, Defendant subjected Plaintiffto fabricated discipline for conduct that had supposedly occurred prior to Plaintiff's complaint of discrimination.
Plaintiff had not been disciplined by Defendant prior to this June 26, 2018 discipline.
Following Plaintiff's June 4, 2018 request for a religious accommodation, Plamtiff followed-up on the request numerous times.
Despite this, Plaintiff did not receive a response to his request during the time he was employed by Defendant.
Following the fabricated discipline on June 26, 2018, Defendant continued to harass Plaintiff.

Specifically, Defendant’s supervisors began aggressively monitoring Plaintiff and disparaging his performance, Additionally, Plaintiff was still not allowed to pray at work, despite the fact that employees of other religions and/or races were allowed to do so. On or around August 23, 2018, Defendant advised Plaintiff that it would be changing his schedule so that, for the first time in Plaintiff's employment with Defendant, Plaintiff would be unable to maintain his second job. Plaintiff reported to Defendant that he believed this action was retaliatory.
Following this, Defendant continued to subject Plaintiff to harassment.
On or around September 20, 2018, Plaintiff was constructively terminated from employment with Defendant.

sections.name: PRAYER FOR RELIEF
sentences: WHEREFORE, Plaintiff, George Smith, requests that the Court grant him the following relief against Defendant: (a) Damages for past and future monetary losses as a result of Defendant’s unlawful discrimination; Case 2:19-cv-03150-CSMW Document1 Filed 07/19/19 Page 11 of 12 (b) (c) (d) (e) (f) (g) (h) (i) Q) (k) ) Compensatory damages; Punitive damages; Liquidated damages; Emotional pain and suffering; Reasonable attorneys’ fees; Recoverable costs; Pre and post judgment interest; An allowance to compensate for negative tax consequences; A permanent injunction enjoining Defendant, its directors, officers, employees, apents, successors, heirs and assigns, and all persons in active concert or participation with them, from engaging in, ratifying, or refusing to correct, employment practices which discriminate in violation of TITLE VII, the PHRA, Section 1981 and the United States Constitution.

Order Defendant to remove and expunge, or to cause to be removed and expunged, all negative, discriminatory, and/or defamatory memoranda and documentation from Plaintiff's record of employment, including, but not limited, the pre-textual reasons cited for her adverse actions, disciplines, and termination; and Awarding extraordinary, equitable and/or injunctive relief as permitted by law, equity and the federal statutory provisions sued hereunder, pursuant to Rules 64 and 65 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. ey Of ot Gregg Eva C.
